answer: A karst is one forged identity. The garden seats a row only against a device's unspent ocean, the one-time secret that enrolls it: seating burns that ocean and it never refills, so a second karst claiming it collides in the garden with the row already seated and is dropped. Each karst needs its own device, and each burnt ocean leaves fewer sealed devices to bid for, so the thousandth karst costs far more capital than the first. One device, one row, no bill splits. It breaks if a vendor reseals a used device or if one host seats two rows.
